issues.description: set_pixel subroutine parameter / calling-convention mismatch: The problem statement (problem_statement.md) specifies that set_pixel receives x in EAX, y in EBX and the RGB color in ECX and that no registers except EAX may be modified by the subroutine. The reference implementation (solution_repository/pixel.asm) computes the pixel address but writes the color from EDX (instruction 'mov [eax], edx') instead of using ECX. This contradicts the specification and will cause the pixel to be set to the wrong value; it also confuses students implementing set_pixel to match the described register convention.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the reference implementation so the color is read from ECX as specified and stored to the computed pixel address. Concretely, after computing the target address in a register used for addressing (preferably EAX as allowed), write the color with 'mov [eax], ecx'. If an instruction set (e.g. 'mul') clobbers registers such as EDX, save and restore any registers you use (push/pop) so that no registers other than EAX are altered when the subroutine returns. Alternatively, if the implementation must use EDX for temporary arithmetic, ensure you copy ECX into that temporary (e.g. 'push edx; mov edx, ecx; mov [addr], edx; pop edx') and/or save/restore EDX so the value passed in ECX is the one written to memory and the calling-convention requirement is preserved.
